en.explanation: The simplest of all strokes - a single horizontal stroke stands for the number one. It forms the basis of many kanji such as 三 (three) and 上 (up).
Two curved strokes reminiscent of human legs. Used as the bottom element in 元 (origin), 兄 (older brother) and 光 (light).
A plant growing out of the earth - symbolizes life and growth. 生 is versatile: "live", "be born", "raw". Appears in 産 (production) and 用 (use).
A fence or frame - symbolizes use and application. 用 itself means "use" and is its own radical.
A rice field divided into four plots, seen from above. As たへん (side form) in 男 (man - one who works in the field), 町 (town district), 界 (boundary), 番 (number).
Represents a roll of fabric or cloth. Appears in 疎 (estranged) and 疑 (doubt).
A person lying on a bed - symbolizes illness. Surrounds kanji such as 病 (illness), 痛 (pain), 療 (healing) and 癒 (recover).
Two feet walking apart. Appears in 発 (fire/depart) and 登 (climb) - both require the first step.
A drop of sunlight - the color white as a symbol of purity and clarity. Appears in 百 (hundred), 的 (target), 皆 (all) and 皇 (emperor).
A hand stripping off a hide. Not to be confused with 革 (leather, radical 177). 皮 stands for raw, untreated skin. Appears in 波 (wave).
A flat plate or bowl seen from the side. Appears in 盆 (tray/Obon festival), 益 (benefit), 盗 (steal) and 監 (supervise).
An eye turned on its side. As めへん (side form) in 直 (direct), 看 (nurse/watch), 着 (wear/arrive), 知 (know) and 研 (polish/research).
Shows two strokes converging, symbolizing entering. Appears in 全 (whole/all) and 内 (inside).
A long spear. The kanji 矛 is known from the word 矛盾 (mujun - contradiction), literally "spear and shield" - a famous Chinese parable.
An arrow with tip and shaft. Appears in 知 (know - an arrow hitting its target) and 短 (short).
A boulder under a cliff. As いしへん (side form) in 研 (polish/research), 破 (break), 確 (certain/confirm) and 磁 (magnet).
An altar on which offerings are made to the gods. As しめすへん (side form) in religious kanji: 社 (shrine/company), 神 (god), 禁 (prohibited), 福 (fortune), 祈 (pray).
Represents an animal track. In 寓, 禸 lies within the component 禺. The main radical of 寓 is 宀.
A grain plant with a drooping ear. As のぎへん (side form) in 私 (I), 科 (subject), 秋 (autumn - harvest time), 種 (kind/seed), 積 (accumulate).
A roof over an opening - a cave or hole. As あなかんむり (top form) in 空 (empty/sky), 究 (investigate), 突 (thrust), 窓 (window).
A person standing upright on the ground. Appears in 章 (chapter), 端 (end/edge) and 競 (compete).
Two bamboo leaves - bamboo is a symbol of flexibility and strength. As たけかんむり (top form) in 第 (ordinal prefix), 等 (class/equal), 答 (answer), 算 (calculate), 管 (pipe/manage).
Grains of rice around a stalk - rice as Japan's staple food. Appears in 米 (rice/America), 精 (essence/refined) and 粉 (powder/flour).
Two diverging strokes symbolize the number eight, considered a lucky number in Japanese because it "opens out". Contained in 公 (public) and 六 (six).
Silk threads from a cocoon. As いとへん (side form) very common in 約 (promise), 索 (rope), 細 (fine), 終 (end), 経 (experience).
A large clay jar for storage. A rare radical - 缶 today also means "can".
A net seen from above - as あみがしら (top form) in kanji related to catching and arranging: 置 (place), 署 (office) and 罪 (crime).
A sheep with horns seen from the front. Sheep were considered gentle and beautiful, hence in 美 (beautiful) and 群 (group/flock).
Two feathers or wings. In 羽 (feather), 習 (learn - birds practice flying) and 翼 (wing).
An old man with a staff and long hair. In 老 (old), 考 (think - the wisdom of age) and 者 (person).
A strand of beard on the chin - symbolizes "and yet" or "but". Appears in 耐 (endure).
A plow working the earth. In 耕 (plow) and 耗 (consume) - both connected with agricultural work.
An ear seen from the side. As みみへん (side form) in 聞 (hear), 職 (occupation) and 聖 (holy) - all connected with listening and understanding.
A hand holding a brush. Appears as a component in 書 (write) - writing with a brush.
An enclosure open at the bottom, surrounding something from above and the sides. Found in 内 (inside), 冊 (volume) and 再 (again).
Strips of meat. As にくづき (side form) it looks like 月 (moon), but means body/flesh. In 肩 (shoulder), 育 (raise), 背 (back), 能 (ability), 腕 (arm).
A kneeling person with a lowered gaze - a subject before his ruler. In 臣 (vassal) and 臨 (attend/face).
Originally a nose - in Japan people point to their own nose to say "myself". 自 means "self".
An arrow reaching its target - symbolizes arriving and reaching. Appears in 致 (bring about).
A mortar for pounding rice or medicine. Appears in 興 (interest/flourish).
A tongue sticking out of the mouth. 舌 appears in 舗 (shop/pave) - the tongue for tasting and speaking.
Two feet pointing against each other - symbolizes dancing or going toward one another. Appears in 舞 (dance).
A boat seen from the side. As ふねへん (side form) in 船 (ship), 航 (navigation) and 艦 (warship).
Symbolizes something good or the stopping of an action. Appears as a component in 良 (good) and 色 (color).
Originally a kneeling person together with another - symbolizes beauty and color. 色 means "color".
A roof sign reminiscent of a crown or covering. It sits above characters related to protection or covering, such as 写 (write/copy) and 軍 (army).
Two blades of grass as a roof over plant kanji. One of the most common radicals: 花 (flower), 英 (excellent), 茶 (tea), 草 (grass), 薬 (medicine).
Tiger stripes - represents a crouching tiger. As とらがしら (top form) in 虚 (empty/vain) and 虎 (tiger).
A snake or insect - in ancient China, "insect" covered all small creeping animals. As むしへん (side form) in many animal names.
A vessel with blood in it. 血 itself means "blood". Appears in words such as 血液 (blood) and 出血 (bleeding).
A crossroads - symbolizes going and rows. As ぎょうがまえ (enclosing form) in 行 (go), 術 (technique), 街 (street) and 表 (surface).
A garment with collar and sleeves. As ころもへん (side form) in 被 (suffer), 装 (equip), 裏 (reverse side), 補 (supplement), 複 (double).
A bird's nest - birds return at sunset (in the west). As a roof shape in 要 (need), 覆 (cover) and 見 (see).
A large eye on legs - active seeing and observing. In 見 (see), 親 (parent/close), 観 (view), 規 (rule) and 覚 (awaken).
An animal horn - also symbolizes corners and angles. In 角 (angle/horn), 解 (solve/understand) and 触 (touch).
Sound waves coming from a mouth. As ごんべん (side form) one of the most important radicals: 言 (say), 計 (plan), 記 (write down), 話 (speak), 読 (read).
Two strokes on the left representing frozen water (ice) - in contrast to さんずい (three strokes = water). Appears in 冬 (winter), 冷 (cold) and 凍 (frozen).
Water flowing between mountains - a valley. 谷 itself means "valley" and is a kanji in its own right.
A vessel with beans in it. Appears in 豊 (abundant/plentiful) and 短 (short) - beans as a symbol of abundance.
A pig or wild boar. Appears in 家 (house - pigs once lived in the house) and 象 (elephant).
A cat-like predator. Appears in 貞 (chaste/faithful) and 貨 (goods/currency).
A shell - used as a means of payment in ancient China. As かいへん (side form) in money kanji: 販 (sell), 買 (buy), 資 (capital), 質 (quality), 贈 (give as a gift).
Earth and fire make the color red. 赤 itself means "red" and also symbolizes sincerity.
A running person with swinging arms. As そうにょう (enclosing form) in 走 (run), 起 (get up), 超 (surpass) and 趣 (taste/charm).
A knee and a foot - symbolizes walking and stepping. As あしへん (side form) in 足 (foot), 路 (road), 踏 (step on) and 踊 (dance).
A pregnant body seen from the side - symbolizes the whole body. 身 means "body" or "oneself".
A cart seen from above: axle, wheels and body. As くるまへん (side form) in 車 (car), 転 (turn/fall over), 載 (load) and 輪 (wheel/ring).
Represents a small table or stool. A rare radical that appears in 凡 (ordinary) and as an element in 風 (wind).
A tattooing needle tool - symbolizes punishment and sharpness. Appears in 辛 (spicy), 辞 (word/quit) and 辰 (dragon/morning).
The fifth zodiac sign (dragon) - stands for the morning hours. Appears in 農 (agriculture).
A foot on a road - symbolizes movement. One of the most common radicals: 近 (near), 送 (send), 通 (pass through), 速 (fast), 進 (advance).
Stands on the right and symbolizes a town or settlement. In 部 (department), 都 (capital), 郵 (mail) and 郎 (young man).
A wine jar - symbolizes alcohol and fermentation. In 酌 (pour), 配 (distribute) and 酒 (sake/alcohol).
Grain being sorted and distinguished. Appears in 釈 (explain/release) and 重 (heavy/important).
Field and earth make a village. Also a unit of length (about 4 km). In 重 (heavy), 野 (field) and 量 (quantity/measure).
Gold nuggets in the earth. As かねへん (side form) one of the most common radicals for metals: 鉄 (iron), 銀 (silver), 録 (record), 鏡 (mirror).
An old man with long hair - symbolizes length and time. 長 means both "long" and "chief/head".
Two door leaves - a large gate. As もんがまえ (enclosing form) in 門 (gate), 間 (interval), 開 (open), 関 (relation) and 閲 (review).
A box open at the top that receives something. Appears in 出 (go out) and 函 (box).
Steps of a hill - stands on the left. In contrast to おおざと (right = town). In 防 (defend), 限 (limit), 院 (institution), 際 (occasion), 陸 (land).
A captured person - symbolizes subjugation and dependence. Appears in 難 (difficult).
A bird with a short tail - in contrast to 鳥 (bird with a long tail). In 集 (gather), 雑 (mixed) and 離 (separate).
Raindrops falling from clouds. As あめかんむり (top form) in weather kanji: 雪 (snow), 雲 (cloud), 電 (electricity) and 雷 (thunder).
Plants and clear water - the color blue-green. Appears in 青 (blue/green), 静 (quiet/calm) and 清 (pure).
Two halves that repel each other - symbolizes negation and error. 非 means "not" or "wrong".
A face in a frame - symbolizes surface and face. 面 means "face" as well as "surface" or "mask".
Tanned leather - in contrast to 皮 (raw skin). In 革 (leather/revolution), 鞍 (saddle) and 靴 (shoes).
Softly tanned leather - finer than 革. Appears in 韓 (Korea) and 韻 (rhyme/tone).
A chive plant. In the Japanese character 韮 (Chinese chive), 韭 stands under the grass component 艹.
Represents a Japanese sword. As りっとう (side form on the right) it appears in many kanji meaning cutting or separating: 分 (divide), 切 (cut), 別 (separate).
A mouth with sound waves - symbolizes sound and tone. 音 (sound/tone) appears in 響 (resound/echo).
A head on a body. As おおがい (right side) in 頂 (summit), 順 (order), 頼 (request), 題 (topic) and 顔 (face).
An insect in the wind - in ancient China people believed insects arose from the wind. 風 means "wind" and also "style".
A crane with spread wings in flight. 飛 means "fly" and is one of the most complex single-syllable kanji.
A lid over a bowl of rice - food. As しょくへん (side form) in 飲 (drink), 養 (nourish), 館 (hall/building) and 餅 (rice cake).
A head with hair - symbolizes the neck as the link between head and body. 首 means "neck" and "leader".
Grain and sweet scent - the pleasant smell of ripe grain. 香 means "fragrance" and "incense".
A horse seen from the side with mane and legs. As うまへん (side form) in 馬 (horse), 駅 (station), 駐 (park), 騒 (make noise) and 験 (experience/test).
Bones and joints of a skeleton. 骨 means "bone" and appears as a component in 體/体 (body).
A tall building with a tower - symbolizes height. 高 means "tall" and also "expensive".
A bent arm symbolizes power and strength. Common in kanji such as 加 (add), 労 (labor/toil), 動 (move) and 勉 (exert oneself).
Long, hanging hair. Appears in 髪 (hair) - the hair on a person's head.
Two fighters facing each other. The rare character 鬨 (battle cry) contains 鬥. The other kanji 闘 (fight), in contrast, uses 門.
A vessel for ritual sacrificial wine at ceremonies. A rare radical; appears in 鬯.
A three-legged bronze cauldron for cooking. As a component, 鬲 is visible in 隔 and 融; their main radicals are 阝 and 虫 respectively.
A ghost with a large head and horns. Appears in 魂 (soul) and 魅 (charm/enchant) - the supernatural world.
A fish with head, body and tail fin. As うおへん (side form) in 魚 (fish), 鮮 (fresh) and 鯨 (whale).
A bird with a long tail - in contrast to 隹 (short-tailed bird). In 鳥 (bird), 鶏 (chicken) and many bird names.
Represents salt. Visible in 鹽, the traditional Japanese spelling of 塩 (salt). The modern form 塩 is classified under 土.
A deer with antlers. Appears in 鹿 (deer) and 麗 (beautiful/elegant) - deer were considered graceful animals.
A wheat plant with an ear. 麦 means "wheat" or "barley" - important cereal crops.
A single vertical stroke that appears as a basic element in many kanji. It symbolizes a line passing through and is found in 中 (middle) and 串 (skewer).
An enclosing shape representing wrapping or enveloping. Appears in 包 (wrap) and 化 (transform).
Hemp plants under a roof - hemp was used for weaving textiles. 麻 means "hemp" and also "numbness".
The color yellow - the imperial color in ancient China. 黄 means "yellow" and symbolizes the earth and the center.
A millet plant. The character 黎 (dark) is listed in the dictionary under 黍. The reading レイ is an on reading of the kanji.
Soot above a fire - the color black. 黒 means "black". Appears in 黙 (be silent) - being quiet in the dark.
A rare radical for embroidery. The historical Japanese characters 黼 and 黻 denote embroidery or embroidered patterns; they occur mainly in classical texts.
A frog or toad. The rare character 鼈 (soft-shelled turtle) is classified under this radical; the usual everyday spelling is すっぽん.
A three-legged ritual vessel made of bronze. 鼎 itself is a Japanese kanji; the rare character 鼐 also denotes a three-legged vessel.
A drum on a stand. 鼓 means "drum" and also "encourage/stir up" - the drumbeat motivates.
A mouse or rat - the first animal in the Chinese zodiac. 鼠 symbolizes cleverness and adaptability.
A nose from the front - the most prominent feature of the face. 鼻 means "nose". In Japan people point to the nose to say "me".
Represents a spoon or utensil. Appears in 化 (transform) and 北 (north) - in 北 two people sit back to back.
Ears of grain at the same height - symbolizes uniformity and order. Appears in 斉 (equal) and 斎 (purification/abstinence).
Teeth in a mouth - symbolizes age and maturity (teeth as a sign of growth). Appears in 歯 (tooth) and 齢 (age).
A dragon - the most powerful mythical creature in East Asian mythology. A symbol of imperial power, good fortune and rain. 龍/竜 means "dragon".
A turtle - a symbol of longevity and wisdom. Turtle shells were used in divination. 亀 means "turtle".
A flute; the last of the 214 Kangxi radicals. Visible as the right-hand component in 鑰, a rare Japanese character for key. The main radical of 鑰 is 金.
A box open to the right that encloses something. Appears in 区 (ward), 医 (medicine) and 匹 (counter for animals).
Similar to radical 22, but with a concealed opening. A rare radical in 区 (ward) and 匹 (counter for animals).
A cross of a horizontal and a vertical stroke stands for the number ten. Contained in 千 (thousand), 半 (half) and 南 (south).
Represents the cracks in a turtle shell that were interpreted in ancient divination. Appears in 占 (fortune-telling) and 卓 (outstanding).
Represents an official seal or one half of a tally stick. Appears in 印 (seal/print), 危 (dangerous) and 卵 (egg).
An overhanging cliff or rock ledge. This radical covers the rest of the character like a roof, e.g. in 原 (origin/plain) and 厳 (strict).
Symbolizes something private or turned away. Appears in 去 (leave), 参 (take part) and 反 (opposite).
Represents a right hand and means "again" or "also". Common in 友 (friend), 取 (take) and 受 (receive).
A single dot, the smallest building block of kanji writing. It appears as an accent in many characters such as 主 (master) and 丹 (cinnabar red).
A square represents an open mouth. One of the most common radicals - it appears in kanji for speaking, eating and openings: 名 (name), 味 (taste), 和 (harmony).
A closed square that completely surrounds something - like a wall around a city. Appears in 国 (country), 回 (turn), 図 (diagram) and 団 (group).
A cross on a base line symbolizes a mound of earth. As つちへん (side form) in 地 (earth/ground), 場 (place/spot), 増 (increase) and many others.
Similar to 土 (earth), but the upper stroke is longer. Stands for a scholar or warrior (samurai). Appears in 売 (sell) and 声 (voice).
Literally "winter head" - the top component of some kanji. Appears in 夏 (summer) and 外 (outside). Despite the name, it has no direct connection to winter.
A rare radical for walking slowly. The historical character 夐 (distant) is listed in the dictionary under this radical.
A crescent moon symbolizes evening and twilight. Appears in 外 (outside), 多 (many), 夜 (night) and 夢 (dream).
A person with outstretched arms symbolizes greatness. A very common radical in 天 (sky), 太 (fat), 夫 (husband) and 奨 (encourage).
Represents a kneeling woman. As おんなへん (side form) in kanji related to women or their qualities: 好 (like), 妹 (younger sister), 妻 (wife).
Shows a small child with outstretched arms. Appears in 字 (character), 学 (learn) and 季 (season) - learning begins in childhood.
A diagonal stroke from top right to bottom left. This basic stroke appears in kanji such as 久 (long-lasting) and 乏 (scarce).
A roof over the kanji - symbolizes house and shelter. Very common in 安 (safe/cheap), 完 (complete), 定 (decide), 実 (fruit/truth), 室 (room).
Represents a traditional unit of length (about 3 cm). Symbolizes precision and measure. Appears in 対 (opposite), 専 (exclusively) and 導 (guide).
Three strokes - a center point that divides - symbolize something small. Appears in 少 (few) and 尖 (pointed).
Represents a bent or lame leg. As a roof element in 尻 (buttocks), 尾 (tail), 届 (deliver), 屋 (house/shop) and 展 (exhibit).
Originally a lying body. Today it serves as a roof shape in kanji for body parts and rooms: 尻 (buttocks), 尾 (tail), 局 (bureau), 屋 (house), 展 (exhibit).
Represents a young plant shoot. 屯 (camp) is an example of the dictionary classification under this rare radical.
Three peaks symbolize a mountain. As やまへん (side form) in many nature kanji: 岳 (peak), 島 (island), 崎 (cape), 峠 (mountain pass).
Three flowing lines represent a river. Appears in 州 (province/state) and 巣 (nest). One of the most vivid pictograms.
Two horizontal strokes joined by a vertical one - a tool or workpiece. Appears in 左 (left) and 巨 (huge).
A winding sign that points to one's own person. Appears in 巳 (snake, 6th zodiac sign) and 巴 (comma shape).
Originally the second sign in the Chinese cycle of ten. Its curved shape resembles a hook and is found in 九 (nine) and 乾 (dry).
A hanging cloth or strip of fabric. As はばへん (side form) in kanji for textiles and surfaces: 市 (city/market), 布 (cloth), 希 (hope), 帝 (emperor), 帯 (belt).
A pestle or rammer - symbolizes drying and influence. Appears in 平 (flat/peace), 年 (year) and 幸 (happiness).
Tiny threads symbolize something fine or small. Appears in 幻 (illusion) and 幼 (childlike/young).
A slanted roof covering the rest of the character from the upper left. Appears in building kanji: 広 (wide), 店 (shop), 府 (government seat), 度 (degree), 床 (floor).
Represents a long stride or march. Appears in 建 (build) and 延 (extend) - both require movement.
Two ten-signs make twenty. Appears in 弁 (distinguish/valve) and 弄 (toy with).
Represents the shaft of a crossbow. Appears in 式 (ceremony/formula) and 引 (pull).
A drawn bow. As ゆみへん (side form) in 引 (pull), 弱 (weak), 強 (strong) and 張 (stretch) - all connected with the tension of a bow.
Literally "pig's head" - a head-part radical. Appears in 当 (hit/in charge) and 形 (shape).
Three parallel diagonal strokes on the right side - symbolize patterns, light or decoration. In 形 (shape), 彩 (coloring) and 影 (shadow).
A small hook that sits like a roof over other elements. It appears in 了 (finish) and 予 (in advance).
Shows a foot on a road - stands for walking and movement. Very common: 後 (after), 待 (wait), 徒 (on foot), 得 (obtain), 復 (return).
Represents the heart - the seat of feelings and thoughts. As りっしんべん (side form) or したごころ (bottom form) in 念 (thought), 思 (think), 情 (feeling), 感 (feel), 意 (intention).
A pole weapon - the halberd. Appears in kanji related to war and fighting: 成 (become/succeed), 我 (I), 戦 (war/battle), 戯 (play).
A single-leaf door (in contrast to 門, the double-leaf gate). Appears in 所 (place), 戻 (return), 房 (room) and 扇 (fan).
A hand with spread fingers. As てへん (side form) one of the most common radicals: 打 (hit), 持 (hold), 指 (finger/point), 探 (search), 推 (push).
A branch or twig that splits off. Appears in 改 (change) and 放 (release) - branches off the main path.
A hand holding a stick - symbolizes striking or acting upon. Right-hand side in 改 (change), 放 (release), 教 (teach) and 整 (arrange).
Originally a tattooed or patterned mark - stands for writing and culture. Appears in 斉 (equal) and 斑 (spot).
A ladle or dry measure (about 18 liters). Also the constellation "Big Dipper". Appears in 料 (fee/material) and 斜 (slanted).
An axe for felling wood. Appears in 新 (new) - literally: felling a new tree with an axe -, 断 (cut off) and 施 (carry out).
Two horizontal strokes one above the other form the number two. This simple tally principle is typical of the early numerals.
Represents a plow or an indication of direction. Appears in 旅 (journey) and 族 (tribe/family) - movement in one direction.
Means "not present" or negation. Appears as a component in 既 (already) and 早 (early). A rare radical.
A circle with a dot in the middle - the sun. One of the most important radicals: 明 (bright), 時 (time), 曜 (day of the week), 書 (write), 最 (most).
Similar to 日 (sun), but wider - an open mouth speaking. Appears in 更 (further/renew) and 替 (replace).
A crescent moon - stands for the moon and months. As つきへん it is often confused with にくづき (flesh), since both look the same. In 有 (have), 服 (clothing), 朝 (morning), 期 (period).
A tree with trunk, branches and roots. As きへん (side form) in wood and plant kanji: 本 (book/origin), 村 (village), 林 (grove), 楽 (pleasure), 機 (machine).
A person with an open mouth - yawning or calling out. Stands on the right in kanji and often means lack or longing. In 次 (next), 歌 (song) and 欲 (desire).
A footprint that stands still - symbolizes stopping and walking. In 正 (correct), 歩 (walk), 歴 (history) and 死 (death - the stopping of life).
Bone splinters symbolize death and decay. Not to be confused with 月 (moon). Appears in 死 (death), 残 (remain) and 段 (step).
A striking weapon or club - stands on the right in 段 (step/stage) and 殿 (palace/lord). Symbolizes controlled violence.
Literally "pot lid" - this radical sits on top of the rest of the character like a lid. It is found in 交 (cross), 京 (capital) and 親 (parents).
Means "do not" as a prohibition. Related to 母 (mother), but with a different cross stroke. Appears in 毎 (every time) and 毒 (poison).
Two people side by side - they are being compared. The kanji 比 itself means "compare" and is also its own radical.
Represents hair or fur - a tuft of hair on a body. The kanji 毛 itself means hair and is its own radical.
Originally a spoon or spatula - later used for "clan" or "family". Appears in 民 (people), where many families form a people.
Rising clouds of steam - the outer enclosure of 気 (spirit/energy/air). A rare radical found in only a few kanji.
A flowing stream with splashes. As さんずい (three drops on the left) one of the most common radicals: 池 (pond), 海 (sea), 深 (deep), 温 (warm), 漢 (China/kanji).
Flames rising up. As ひへん (side form) or れんが (four dots at the bottom) in 点 (point), 焼 (burn), 熱 (heat) and 照 (illuminate).
A grasping claw or talon from above. As つめかんむり (top form) in kanji expressing grasping or seizing.
A hand holding an axe - a symbol of the father as protector and worker. The kanji 父 means "father".
Two crossed strokes - also called "mixture" or "interweaving". A rare radical that appears as a component in 片 (piece).
One of the most common radicals. As にんべん (亻, side form) it stands on the left in kanji related to people: 仕 (serve), 他 (other), 体 (body). On top, as ひとやね (𠆢), it appears e.g. in 今 (now) and 会 (meet).
The left half of a split piece of wood. Visible in the traditional character 牆 (wall); this is a rare Japanese spelling.
The right half of a split piece of wood. As a standalone kanji 片 means "piece" or "side". Partner of radical 90.
Represents a fang or tusk. A rare radical - 牙 itself means "canine tooth".
A cow's head with horns seen from the front. As うしへん (side form) in 物 (thing), 牧 (pasture) and 特 (special) - cattle were valuable property.
A dog with a raised tail. As けものへん (side form) in 状 (condition), 独 (alone), 猿 (monkey) and 獣 (beast) - animals and animal behavior.
Symbolizes the dark, mysterious and profound. Appears in 率 (rate/ratio) and as a component in 王 (king).
玉 means jade or gem and has five strokes. The common side form 王 has four strokes. As たまへん (side form) in 現 (present), 理 (reason), 環 (ring) and 玉 (gem).
Represents a melon - the vines and the fruit. A rare radical; 瓜 itself means "melon" or "gourd".
Represents fired clay tiles. Appears in 瓶 (bottle). Roof tiles (瓦) were an important building material in ancient Japan.
Something sweet in the mouth - the horizontal stroke inside the mouth sign symbolizes the sweet taste. 甘 itself means "sweet" and is a rare radical.
